attributes.DMU_100K_DESCRIPTION: Coarsely crystalline white marble with gray streaks. Locally associated with calc-silicate granofels and schist. Also found as small lenses in the banded gneiss, schist, and amphibolite.

attributes.DMU_100K_FULL_NAME: eastern melange belt, rocks of the
attributes.DMU_100K_DESCRIPTION: Highly deformed chert and medium- to fine-grained banded biotite quartzite (metachert) mixed with tectonized greenstone, greenstone breccia, and marble. Includes hornblende schist and muscovite, biotite quartz schist and dikes of metadiorite and metagabbro. Rare deformed pillows. Locally prehnite in veins. Mostly massive and rarely bedded, greenschist (metabasalt and meta-andesite), metagraywacke, chert-rich metagrit, and metaconglomerate. Medium-grained, light-blue-gray sandstone, with minor amounts of black to brown, fine-grained sandstone, siltstone, argillite, and generally very thin bedded, black to gray chert are also present. Greenstone makes up from 20-50 percent of melange and contains relict clinopyroxene (some titaniferous) and plagioclase in an altered matrix of chlorite, carbonate minerals, and pumpellyite. Original sedimentary and volcanic textures largely obscured by penetrative deformation, low-grade regional metamorphism, and static thermal metamorphism. Contact metamorphism by Tertiary plutons has destroyed original textures and structures as well as earlier formed greenschist-facies minerals; many rocks are now pyroxene hornfels. Lithologically resembles the Upper Jurassic and Lower Cretaceous Constitution terrane in the San Juan Islands. Radiolarians in chert have been dated as Late Jurassic in age. The lithologies suggest a volcanic-arc source for this unit.

attributes.DMU_100K_FULL_NAME: Eastern melange belt of Tabor and others (1993)
attributes.DMU_100K_DESCRIPTION: Abundant mafic volcanic rocks, chert, argillite, lithofeldspathic sandstone, and minor conglomerate and thin tuff; structurally above the western melange belt; unfoliated to weakly foliated.

Monolithologic breccia composed of angular sandstone clasts as much as 10 m across, derived from the Swauk Formation. Rare volcanic clasts. East of Spade Lake, breccia is locally highly sheared and altered. Basal sandstone breccia with lapilli tuff matrix has been described.

attributes.DMU_100K_FULL_NAME: eastern melange belt, rocks of the
attributes.DMU_100K_DESCRIPTION: Lenticular beds and pods of banded, white to grayish, medium- to fine-grained crystalline marble that is locally intercalated with metachert, metagabbro, and greenstone. Includes minor fine-grained pale-green silica carbonate replacement masses.

attributes.DMU_100K_FULL_NAME: western melange belt, rocks of the
attributes.DMU_100K_DESCRIPTION: Black to bluish-gray marble and, in part, interbedded chert and shale occurring as steeply dipping pods and lenticular beds. Thin, green tuffaceous chert beds crop out in marble at Haystack quarry on Proctor Creek.

attributes.DMU_100K_FULL_NAME: eastern melange belt, rocks of the
attributes.DMU_100K_DESCRIPTION: Gray to white, lenticular beds and pods of banded medium- to fine-grained crystalline marble intercalated with metachert and greenstone, locally with chlorite; coarsely crystalline. In part, shaley laminations or graphitic impurities mark bedding planes. Silicified replacement masses. The deposits south of White Horse are mostly in small pods.
